scenarios.hypothesis: A serialized discriminator that passes syntax and schema validation must not authorize construction until normalization, resolver identity, registry generation, and canonical runtime type identity all match the approved reconstruction policy.
scenarios.safe_oracle: Use a controlled local decoder with a mock type registry, synthetic discriminator values, inert fixture classes, and a read-only canary result so no real capability or external system is touched.
scenarios.positive_control: An approved synthetic discriminator under the current schema and current registry generation must resolve to the intended inert data class and return the expected read-only canary receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: Keep parser bytes and schema validity constant but map a neighboring synthetic alias to a non-approved inert type; policy must reject the canonical resolved identity before object construction.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if validation would require a real production object graph, external network effect, arbitrary command or file action, secret material, persistence, destructive behavior, or any unauthorized target.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, policy evaluates the canonical resolved runtime identity and rejects the previously accepted alias while the intended current-generation synthetic data type still reconstructs successfully.
scenarios.artifact_origin: The artifact is generated by a deterministic local fixture representing a lower-authority sender and carries a unique synthetic case identifier rather than any production user or service data.
scenarios.envelope_authentication_context: The fixture envelope is either explicitly unauthenticated or signed by a synthetic principal whose authority is limited to ordinary data fields, making authenticity scope separate from type-selection authority.
scenarios.format_parser_identity: Use one pinned local serializer/parser implementation and configuration for both positive and negative controls so parser-version or format differences cannot explain the registry-resolution outcome.
scenarios.canonical_field_state: Record the parser output after normalization as a deterministic field map containing the same ordinary data and a controlled discriminator, with canonical values captured before schema/type lookup.
scenarios.schema_identity_version: Pin one synthetic schema identity and version that permits the discriminator field structurally but delegates runtime-type authorization to the explicit reconstruction policy under test.
scenarios.discriminator_state: Compare an approved synthetic alias and a neighboring alias while keeping all unrelated fields equal; record both the serialized selector and its normalized selector before registry lookup.
scenarios.registry_resolver_identity: Use a mock resolver with a stable fixture identity whose alias-to-canonical-type table is explicit, auditable, and independent from the incoming selector string or package-prefix representation.
scenarios.registry_generation: Assign a concrete current registry generation to the resolver table and record it in every decision so stale aliases or prior mappings cannot inherit authority from the current registry state.
scenarios.runtime_type_identity: Resolve each selector to a canonical inert runtime type identity and make authorization depend on that identity rather than the textual alias, namespace prefix, or registry-key spelling alone.
scenarios.object_construction_path: The approved path constructs an inert data-only fixture object through a deterministic factory; the non-approved type must be rejected before allocation or behavior-bearing initialization occurs.
scenarios.hook_callback_surface: Fixture classes expose no harmful behavior; a synthetic marker hook exists only to prove whether construction was entered and writes solely to an in-memory controlled event ledger.
scenarios.secondary_interpretation: Ordinary data fields are not treated as paths, templates, queries, policies, or plugins in this case, isolating canonical type resolution as the security-relevant transition being tested.
scenarios.authority_context: The synthetic sender may submit data conforming to the schema but is not authorized to choose arbitrary runtime classes, so represented data authority is intentionally narrower than resolver capability.
scenarios.requested_reconstructed_capability: The positive request asks only to reconstruct the approved inert data class; the negative alias implicitly requests a neighboring runtime identity outside the sender's permitted reconstruction set.
scenarios.policy_decision: The reconstruction policy binds normalized selector, schema identity/version, canonical runtime type identity, resolver identity, and registry generation into a deterministic allow-or-deny record.
scenarios.effective_reconstructed_authority: Allowed authority is limited to creation of the approved inert data object with no callback, plugin, filesystem, process, or network capability; the neighboring type receives no reconstructed authority.
scenarios.privileged_consumer: The consumer is a mock local object receiver that can inspect the inert fixture and emit a deterministic canary receipt but cannot invoke real privileged services or system-sensitive resources.
scenarios.bounded_result: The successful positive path returns a read-only synthetic canary naming the canonical type; the rejected alias returns an explicit denial and produces no construction marker or external side effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Every canary or denial is bound to the artifact case identifier, schema version, normalized selector, registry generation, canonical runtime type identity, and policy-decision identifier.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: The baseline keeps schema and registry generations fixed, then a paired lifecycle control advances the registry generation to prove old selector mappings are not silently reused as current authority.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Replay the same canonical field map first with the neighboring alias and then under a new registry generation while changing no other field; each unauthorized binding must be rejected independently.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Exclude parser fallback, default-type insertion, schema migration, accidental fixture registration, alias collision, registry reload race, stale event logging, and receipt correlation with another synthetic request.
scenarios.evidence_level: Target evidence is DT5 only when wrong canonical type acceptance reaches a bounded inert result and the complete selector-to-registry-to-type-to-policy chain plus remediation is proven causally.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Without a bounded result and exact canonical type plus registry-generation binding, the evidence ceiling remains below DT4; textual alias acceptance or parser success alone cannot justify DT5.

scenarios.hypothesis: A syntactically valid or correctly authenticated serialized object must not acquire constructor, post-load, callback, plugin, or secondary-interpreter behavior broader than the initiating principal's explicitly approved reconstructed authority.
scenarios.safe_oracle: Use a synthetic authenticated sender, inert callback marker, mock plugin consumer, and controlled in-memory event ledger; the oracle observes only benign marker state and never invokes a real command, file, or network action.
scenarios.positive_control: The approved synthetic data-only type reconstructs with ordinary fields and no behavior marker, or invokes only the explicitly permitted inert callback when the policy grants that exact capability.
scenarios.negative_control: Keep envelope authentication and schema validity unchanged while requesting a neighboring inert hook capability outside the sender's scope; policy must deny it before the behavior boundary executes.
scenarios.stop_condition: Abort and do not proceed if proof would require real command execution, arbitrary file modification, outbound network access, production credentials, persistence, malware, destructive behavior, or a system outside explicit authorization.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, the over-broad synthetic hook or secondary interpretation is blocked while the intended data-only reconstruction and any explicitly allowed inert neighboring behavior continue to work unchanged.
scenarios.artifact_origin: The serialized artifact comes from a deterministic synthetic principal modeled as authorized to submit configuration data but not to choose behavior-bearing callbacks, plugins, resource openers, or privileged interpreters.
scenarios.envelope_authentication_context: A mock signature validates the sender identity and data-submission purpose, deliberately demonstrating that valid authenticity is narrower than authority to select arbitrary reconstructed behavior.
scenarios.format_parser_identity: One pinned parser configuration processes positive and negative artifacts identically through syntax decoding so any later marker difference is attributable to reconstruction policy rather than parsing drift.
scenarios.canonical_field_state: Capture a stable canonical field map whose ordinary values remain equal across controls while one synthetic capability selector requests either data-only behavior or a neighboring inert callback/plugin marker.
scenarios.schema_identity_version: Use a fixed synthetic schema version that accepts the capability-selector field structurally, making the separate reconstruction-policy decision observable instead of hiding the issue behind schema rejection.
scenarios.discriminator_state: The discriminator resolves to the same approved fixture type for both controls; only a behavior-bearing callback or plugin selector changes, isolating post-type-resolution authority as the tested transition.
scenarios.registry_resolver_identity: The runtime type resolver is a mock fixed registry that always selects the same canonical inert fixture class, while a separate controlled callback/plugin registry resolves the requested behavior identity.
scenarios.registry_generation: Record both the type-registry and callback/plugin-registry generations so a benign marker cannot be attributed to stale resolver state or an earlier policy generation reused by the fixture.
scenarios.runtime_type_identity: Both controls reconstruct the same canonical inert runtime type identity, which prevents unexpected class selection from being mistaken for the hook-capability authorization hypothesis.
scenarios.object_construction_path: Construction follows the same deterministic factory and setter sequence for both controls, with behavior activation deferred until policy evaluates the explicit synthetic callback or plugin capability request.
scenarios.hook_callback_surface: The only behavior-bearing surface is an inert callback or mock plugin that appends a canary token to an in-memory ledger, providing proof of invocation without executing harmful or external functionality.
scenarios.secondary_interpretation: A controlled string may later be interpreted as a callback/plugin key only after ordinary schema validation; the trace records this semantic transition separately from the original data representation.
scenarios.authority_context: The synthetic principal owns the data values but has an authenticated scope that excludes arbitrary behavior selection, so data ownership and reconstructed-behavior authority are intentionally distinct.
scenarios.requested_reconstructed_capability: The negative fixture requests one named inert callback/plugin capability outside the principal's approved data-only scope, while the positive control stays within the allowed reconstruction purpose.
scenarios.policy_decision: Policy combines authenticated sender scope, schema identity, canonical runtime type, requested inert behavior identity, registry generation, and consumer context before deciding whether behavior may activate.
scenarios.effective_reconstructed_authority: The positive path receives only data-object authority or the one explicitly permitted inert marker; the negative path must not inherit the decoder or consumer's broader ambient callback/plugin capability.
scenarios.privileged_consumer: A mock reconstruction consumer owns the inert callback/plugin registry and emits deterministic receipts; it has no interface to real filesystem, process, device, credential, or external network capabilities.
scenarios.bounded_result: Authorized reconstruction yields the expected synthetic data receipt, while an improperly authorized hook would yield only an in-memory canary marker; no harmful side effect is needed to prove the boundary.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind each data receipt or canary event to artifact ID, authenticated principal, requested behavior identity, canonical runtime type, policy decision, registry generation, and fixture correlation ID.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: Advance the callback/plugin policy generation in a paired control and verify that a previously permitted synthetic behavior does not survive revocation through cached or restored reconstructed state.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold authenticated sender, parser, schema, and runtime type constant while changing only the requested inert behavior, then hold behavior constant while narrowing sender scope; unauthorized variants must fail.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Exclude expected post-load behavior, accidental marker initialization, callback registry collision, stale in-memory ledger entries, schema-default behavior, debug-only permissiveness, and correlation with another fixture run.
scenarios.evidence_level: DT5 requires a causally bound inert marker or bounded receipt plus complete authenticity, type, hook, authority, policy, lifecycle, counterfactual, and remediation evidence for the same request tuple.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Hook reachability, valid signatures, or callback names without a bounded causally correlated effect remain below DT4; arbitrary-code or system-compromise claims are outside this deterministic evidence ceiling.

scenarios.hypothesis: Schema, registry, policy, plugin, or persisted-object generation changes must invalidate stale reconstruction authority instead of allowing an old serialized artifact to inherit current type mappings or capabilities by logical-name reuse.
scenarios.safe_oracle: Use controlled old/current schema and registry generations, synthetic persisted artifacts, a mock resolver, and an inert read-only canary consumer so lifecycle behavior is observed without real user data or external effects.
scenarios.positive_control: A current-generation synthetic artifact using the current schema, registry mapping, and policy must reconstruct the intended inert data object and produce a fresh correctly bound canary receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: Replay an otherwise identical stale synthetic artifact after the authoritative registry or policy generation advances; the stale generation must be rejected rather than inheriting the current mapping or capability.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop if testing stale reconstruction would require retaining real secrets, production sessions, unauthorized persisted state, arbitrary execution, external network interaction, destructive mutation, persistence, or third-party systems.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After generation-aware remediation, every stale synthetic artifact or resolver binding is rejected while a freshly encoded current-generation artifact preserves the intended data-only reconstruction behavior.
scenarios.artifact_origin: The fixture creates deterministic serialized state before a controlled schema/registry transition and labels it with a synthetic origin and generation so no production session or user-owned artifact is required.
scenarios.envelope_authentication_context: The stale and current artifacts use the same mock authenticated principal, allowing the test to isolate lifecycle invalidation rather than confuse a generation failure with sender-authentication differences.
scenarios.format_parser_identity: Use the same pinned parser implementation across old and current controls, recording any explicit migration step separately so parser replacement cannot explain stale-authority acceptance.
scenarios.canonical_field_state: Normalize old and current artifacts into comparable deterministic field maps with one recorded generation-bearing selector or metadata difference tied to the controlled lifecycle transition.
scenarios.schema_identity_version: Record old and current synthetic schema versions plus compatibility/migration policy; logical schema-name reuse must not erase the security-relevant generation associated with reconstruction authority.
scenarios.discriminator_state: Keep the human-readable discriminator or alias stable across the transition where useful, demonstrating that the same selector text can resolve under different authoritative registry generations.
scenarios.registry_resolver_identity: Use one mock resolver identity whose table is intentionally updated between generations, making the authoritative mapping transition explicit and deterministic rather than dependent on external plugin discovery.
scenarios.registry_generation: Assign monotonic old and current registry generations and include them in every policy and receipt record; stale mappings must not be accepted merely because the alias or class label is unchanged.
scenarios.runtime_type_identity: Record the canonical runtime type selected before and after the controlled transition, including the case where a logical alias is remapped to a neighboring inert type in the new generation.
scenarios.object_construction_path: Current artifacts use the current factory path, while stale artifacts must be rejected before construction if their authoritative schema/registry/policy generation no longer matches the reconstruction context.
scenarios.hook_callback_surface: Any fixture hook is an inert in-memory marker used only to detect whether stale construction crossed the behavior boundary; no real callback, command, file, or network capability is available.
scenarios.secondary_interpretation: If a persisted field is later interpreted as a mock plugin or policy key, record the interpreter generation and require current binding instead of silently reusing stale semantic meaning after migration.
scenarios.authority_context: The synthetic principal remains the same while its allowed reconstruction context advances to the current policy generation, isolating stale lifecycle state from ordinary principal-membership changes.
scenarios.requested_reconstructed_capability: Both stale and current artifacts request the same benign data-only or read-only canary capability, so generation validity is the sole intended security-relevant difference between paired controls.
scenarios.policy_decision: The current policy must bind artifact generation, schema version, registry generation, canonical runtime type, principal scope, and requested capability before any reconstructed object reaches the consumer.
scenarios.effective_reconstructed_authority: Only a current-generation artifact receives narrow data-only or read-only canary authority; stale artifacts receive no reconstructed capability even when their logical names remain syntactically valid.
scenarios.privileged_consumer: The consumer is a mock local state restorer that can return only an inert canary receipt for approved current-generation objects and has no access to real privileged system resources.
scenarios.bounded_result: The current artifact returns a deterministic read-only synthetic canary, while stale artifacts return explicit generation denial and create no construction marker, callback event, or external side effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Each result binds artifact identifier, synthetic principal, schema version, registry generation, policy generation, canonical runtime type, requested capability, and a unique fixture correlation identifier.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: Advance schema, registry, or policy generation through a documented deterministic transition and preserve both old and current fixture identities so stale/current decisions can be compared exactly.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Replay with only the old registry generation, then only the old schema generation, then only the old policy generation while keeping parser, principal, capability, and ordinary data constant.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Exclude migration bugs unrelated to authority, parser fallback, resolver reload races, stale cache telemetry, duplicate fixture identifiers, alias collisions, benign retry behavior, and receipts from previous runs.
scenarios.evidence_level: DT5 requires the bounded canary plus exact old/current generation provenance, canonical type and policy traces, independent lifecycle counterfactuals, alternative elimination, and remediation regression.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Logical-name reuse or observation of stale bytes without a causally bound accepted result stays below DT4; DT5 requires proving stale reconstructed authority across the exact lifecycle chain.
